title: Add HNSW parallel loading support with thread-safe lifecycle management
body:
## Summary

This PR implements parallel loading support for HNSW indexes in the vector extension, addressing critical thread safety and lifecycle management issues.

### Key Changes

1. **Thread-Safe HNSW Index Loading**
   - Added background thread lifecycle management with proper synchronization
   - Implemented `DatabaseLifeCycleManager` to prevent TOCTOU race conditions
   - Fixed transaction management for background loading threads

2. **Catalog Entry Propagation**
   - Updated `Index::load()` interface to accept `CatalogEntry*` parameter
   - Propagated catalog entries through extension framework
   - Enables proper metadata access during index initialization

3. **Transaction Timestamp Persistence**
   - Added `lastTimestamp` persistence in database header
   - Ensures transaction consistency across database restarts
   - Prevents timestamp conflicts during recovery

4. **Index Loading Synchronization**
   - Added index loading wait mechanism for INSERT and COPY FROM operations
   - Implemented synchronous HNSW loading during WAL replay
   - Prevents data corruption from concurrent operations

5. **Bug Fixes**
   - Fixed OverflowFile checkpoint corruption when no data is written
   - Fixed catalog entry handling to prevent infinite loops
   - Added proper error handling and validation

### Test Coverage

- Added `parallel_loading_test.cpp` for HNSW parallel loading scenarios
- Added `overflow_file_checkpoint_test.cpp` for checkpoint edge cases
- All existing tests passing

### Related Issues

- Addresses #6047 (HNSW index loading performance)
- Fixes HNSW parallel loading deadlock issues
- Resolves checkpoint corruption with empty indexes

title: Bug: Segmentation fault on label() of list element
body:
### Kuzu version

v0.11.2

### What operating system are you using?

Ubuntu 24.04

### What happened?

With the following data:

```cypher

CREATE NODE TABLE Person(name STRING PRIMARY KEY, occupation STRING);
CREATE REL TABLE LivesWith(FROM Person TO Person);
CREATE (p:Person {name: 'Alice'})-[:LivesWith]->(:Person {name: 'Bob'});
```

It is possible to extract a label from the path with:

```cypher
MATCH p = (n)-[:LivesWith]->(m:Person {name: 'Bob'})
WITH nodes(p) AS ns
RETURN properties(ns, "_LABEL")[1];
```

But the following segfaults:

```cypher
MATCH p = (n)-[:LivesWith]->(m:Person {name: 'Bob'})
WITH nodes(p) AS ns
RETURN label(ns[1]);
```

title: Bug: Segmentation fault matching on unwound results
body:
**Kuzu v0.11.2, Ubuntu 24.04**


Create a db with a duplicate edge

```cypher
CREATE NODE TABLE Person(name STRING PRIMARY KEY);
CREATE REL TABLE LivesWith(FROM Person TO Person);
CREATE (p:Person {name: 'Alice'});
CREATE (p:Person {name: 'Bob'});
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Alice'}), (q:Person {name: 'Bob'}) CREATE (p)-[:LivesWith]->(q);
MATCH (p:Person {name: 'Alice'}), (q:Person {name: 'Bob'}) CREATE (p)-[:LivesWith]->(q);
```

Then try to delete duplicate edges with the following query:

```cypher
MATCH (a)-[r:LivesWith]->(b)
WITH collect(r) AS rs
WITH rs[2:] AS dups
UNWIND dups AS d
MATCH (a)-[s:LivesWith]->(b)
WHERE s=d
DELETE s;
```
On my system this fails with
```
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

(As a side note, it would be nice to be able to just `DELETE d`, but the binder refuses with `Error: Binder exception: Cannot delete expression d with type VARIABLE. Expect node or rel pattern.`)

title: Fix OverflowFile checkpoint corruption when no data is written
body:
## Description

Fixes #6045

Fixes a critical bug where `OverflowFile::checkpoint()` unconditionally allocated a header page even when no data had been written, causing `PrimaryKeyIndexStorageInfo` corruption and database reopen failures.

## Problem

When creating a VectorIndex without inserting any data, the database checkpoint completes successfully but corrupts the metadata. Reopening the database fails with an assertion error in `hash_index.cpp:487`:

```
KU_ASSERT(hashIndexStorageInfo.overflowHeaderPage == INVALID_PAGE_IDX);
```

### Minimal Reproduction

```cpp
auto db = std::make_unique<Database>("test.db");
auto conn = std::make_unique<Connection>(db.get());

conn->query("CREATE NODE TABLE Item(id STRING PRIMARY KEY, embedding FLOAT[3])");
conn->query("CALL CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX('Item', 'item_idx', 'embedding', metric := 'l2')");

conn.reset();
db.reset();

auto db2 = std::make_unique<Database>("test.db");  // ❌ ASSERTION FAILURE
```

### Root Cause

In `src/storage/overflow_file.cpp:236`, `OverflowFile::checkpoint()` was unconditionally allocating a page even when no data had been written:

```cpp
if (headerPageIdx == INVALID_PAGE_IDX) {
    this->headerPageIdx = getNewPageIdx(&pageAllocator);  // ❌ Allocates even when empty
    headerChanged = true;
}
```

**Sequence of events:**
1. VectorIndex creation creates a `PrimaryKeyIndex` (for STRING primary key)
2. `PrimaryKeyIndex` creates an `OverflowFile` (for strings >12 bytes) with `headerPageIdx = INVALID_PAGE_IDX`
3. During checkpoint, `OverflowFile::checkpoint()` allocates a page unnecessarily
4. This sets `PrimaryKeyIndexStorageInfo.overflowHeaderPage = 1` (should be `INVALID_PAGE_IDX`)
5. Corrupted metadata is serialized to disk
6. On database reopen, assertion fails

## Solution

Skip checkpoint when `headerChanged == false`, following the same design pattern as `NodeTable::checkpoint()` and `RelTable::checkpoint()`:

```cpp
void OverflowFile::checkpoint(PageAllocator& pageAllocator) {
    KU_ASSERT(fileHandle);
    // Skip checkpoint if no data has been written
    if (!headerChanged) {
        return;
    }
    if (headerPageIdx == INVALID_PAGE_IDX) {
        this->headerPageIdx = getNewPageIdx(&pageAllocator);
    }
    // ... rest of checkpoint logic
}
```

The `headerChanged` flag is only set to `true` when actual string data (>12 bytes) is written via `OverflowFileHandle::setStringOverflow()`.

## Benefits

1. ✅ Eliminates metadata corruption
2. ✅ Consistent with system-wide checkpoint design pattern
3. ✅ Reduces unnecessary disk I/O for empty overflow files
4. ✅ Fixes VectorIndex creation without data insertion

## Testing

Added comprehensive test suite in `test/storage/overflow_file_checkpoint_test.cpp` with 5 test cases:

1. `InMemOverflowFileAlwaysAllocatesHeader` - Verifies in-memory behavior
2. `ShortStringsDoNotTriggerOverflow` - Verifies strings ≤12 bytes are inlined
3. `LongStringsDoTriggerOverflow` - Verifies strings >12 bytes use overflow
4. `EmptyOverflowFileHeaderNotChanged` - Documents the core bug fix
5. `VectorIndexCreationSequence` - Documents the bug scenario

All tests pass:
```
[==========] Running 5 tests from 1 test suite.
[  PASSED  ] 5 tests.
```

## Files Changed

- `src/storage/overflow_file.cpp` - Added early return when `headerChanged == false`
- `test/storage/CMakeLists.txt` - Added new test target
- `test/storage/overflow_file_checkpoint_test.cpp` - New test file

## Impact

This fix resolves crashes when:
- Creating a VectorIndex without inserting data
- Using tables with STRING primary keys and no long strings (≤12 bytes)
- Working with empty databases that have indexes

title: [Bug] OverflowFile::checkpoint() corrupts PrimaryKeyIndexStorageInfo when no data has been written

code_snippets.code: KU_ASSERT(hashIndexStorageInfo.overflowHeaderPage == INVALID_PAGE_IDX);

**Why this fix is correct:**

1. `headerChanged` is set to `true` **only** in `OverflowFileHandle::setStringOverflow()` when writing strings >12 bytes
2. If `headerChanged == false`, then `pageWriteCache` is guaranteed to be empty (no data to flush)
3. This follows the same design pattern as other checkpoint methods:
   - `NodeTable::checkpoint()`: `if (!hasChanges) return;`
   - `RelTable::checkpoint()`: `if (!hasChanges) return;`

## Impact

**Affected scenarios:**
- Creating a VectorIndex without inserting data
- Any table with STRING primary key and no long strings (≤12 bytes)
- Empty databases with indexes

**Workaround (before fix):**
Insert at least one record after creating VectorIndex and execute manual `CHECKPOINT`:

This triggers `hasStorageChanges=1`, causing a second checkpoint that re-serializes metadata with correct values.

## Additional Context

**Design Pattern Violation:**

All other components in Kuzu follow the pattern "skip checkpoint when no changes":
- `NodeTable::checkpoint()` checks `hasChanges`
- `RelTable::checkpoint()` checks `hasChanges`
- `OverflowFile::checkpoint()` was the **only exception** that didn't check `headerChanged`

**Benefits of the fix:**
1. ✅ No more metadata corruption
2. ✅ Eliminates unnecessary disk I/O when reopening databases without changes
3. ✅ Consistent with system-wide design pattern
4. ✅ No workaround needed

**Files to modify:**
- `src/storage/overflow_file.cpp` (line 234-254)

## Testing

After applying the fix, the minimal reproduction above should work correctly:

title: Fix thread safety and array bounds issues in local storage structures
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes critical thread safety issues and array out-of-bounds crashes in LocalStorage structures that occur during concurrent operations, particularly during HNSW vector index batch insertions.

## Problem

### Bug Report: Array Out of Bounds Crash During HNSW Index Batch Insert

**Crash Location:**
```cpp
// local_rel_table.cpp:116 in LocalRelTable::delete_
std::vector<DirectedCSRIndex>::operator[] // Out of bounds access
```

**Call Stack:**
```
OnDiskHNSWIndex::shrinkForNode → RelTable::detachDelete 
→ LocalRelTable::delete_ → DirectedCSRIndex vector access (CRASH)
```

**Root Causes:**

1. **Race Condition in Multi-threaded Environment**
   - HNSW index uses multiple worker threads for parallel insertion
   - CSR index state is not properly synchronized across threads during concurrent commitInsert operations
   - Multiple assets inserted in a single transaction trigger parallel HNSW insertions, corrupting CSR index metadata

2. **Missing Bounds Checking**
   - DirectedCSRIndex vector accessed without size validation
   - During shrinkForNode, index calculation assumes CSR vector is pre-allocated, but may not be resized yet in concurrent scenarios

3. **Transaction Isolation Issues**
   - Multiple nodes inserted in single transaction
   - HNSW index attempts to update graph edges before all nodes are committed
   - CSR index metadata (node count, layer sizes) becomes inconsistent

**Reproduction:**
- Batch insert 5+ nodes with vector indices in a single transaction
- Crash rate: 30% (batch=5), 70% (batch=10), ~100% (batch=20+)
- Occurs primarily on multi-core devices during background thread execution

## Solution

### 1. Thread-Safe LocalStorage Access
- Added `tablesMutex` (shared_mutex) for thread-safe table map access
- Implemented double-checked locking pattern in `getOrCreateLocalTable()`
- Renamed `mtx` to `allocatorMutex` for clarity
- Added proper locking in `commit()` and `rollback()` methods

### 2. Thread-Safe LocalNodeTable Operations
- Added `tableMutex` to protect concurrent operations
- Protected all public methods: `insert()`, `update()`, `delete_()`, `clear()`, `validateUniquenessConstraint()`, `lookupPK()`, `addColumn()`

### 3. Thread-Safe LocalRelTable Operations with Bounds Checking
- Added `tableMutex` to protect concurrent operations
- Added `indexMutex` (shared_mutex) to DirectedCSRIndex for fine-grained locking
- **Critical Fix:** Added bounds checking in `delete_()`, `scan()`, and `checkIfNodeHasRels()` to prevent out-of-bounds array access
- Moved `isEmpty()` and `clear()` implementations to .cpp file with proper locking
- Added move constructor/assignment and deleted copy operations for DirectedCSRIndex

### 4. Bounds Checking Implementation
```cpp
// local_rel_table.cpp - delete_() method
auto directedIndexPos = RelDirectionUtils::relDirectionToKeyIdx(deleteState.detachDeleteDirection);
if (directedIndexPos >= directedIndices.size()) {
    // Direction not initialized yet (can happen during HNSW index creation)
    return false;
}
```

## Changes

### LocalStorage (local_storage.h/cpp)
- Added `tablesMutex` (shared_mutex) for thread-safe table map access
- Renamed `mtx` to `allocatorMutex` for clarity
- Implemented double-checked locking pattern in `getOrCreateLocalTable()`
- Added proper locking in `commit()` and `rollback()` methods

### LocalNodeTable (local_node_table.h/cpp)
- Added `tableMutex` to protect concurrent operations
- Protected all public methods

### LocalRelTable (local_rel_table.h/cpp)
- Added `tableMutex` to protect concurrent operations
- Added `indexMutex` (shared_mutex) to DirectedCSRIndex
- **Added bounds checking in `delete_()`, `scan()`, and `checkIfNodeHasRels()`**
- Moved `isEmpty()` and `clear()` to .cpp with proper locking
- Added move semantics for DirectedCSRIndex

## Test Plan

- [x] Added comprehensive thread safety test suite (`local_storage_thread_safety_test.cpp`)
  - `ConcurrentGetOrCreateLocalTable`: Tests thread-safe table creation
  - `ConcurrentInserts`: Tests concurrent insertions across multiple threads
  - `ConcurrentMixedOperations`: Tests mixed read/write operations
  - `RelTableBoundaryCheck`: Tests boundary checking in relationship operations
- [x] Existing tests pass
- [x] Verified with HNSW vector index batch insertions (5-20 nodes per transaction)
- [x] Build succeeds with thread sanitizer (TSAN=TRUE)

## Impact

This fix resolves crashes during:
- Batch vector index insertions (HNSW)
- Concurrent transaction commits
- Multi-threaded query execution with local storage modifications
- DETACH DELETE operations on relationship tables during index reorganization

title: Fix DROP_VECTOR_INDEX persistence bug preventing property updates
body:
# Description

When dropping a vector index via `DROP_VECTOR_INDEX`, the index was correctly removed from the catalog but `NodeTable::dropIndex()` was missing `hasChanges = true`. This caused the table's serialized index list to not be updated during checkpoint, leading to the dropped index persisting across database restarts.

This prevented property updates on previously-indexed columns with the error `"Cannot set property ... because it is used in one or more indexes"`, even though `SHOW_INDEXES()` showed no indexes remaining.

Fixes #6040 

# Contributor agreement

- [x] I have read and agree to the [Contributor Agreement](https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/blob/master/CLA.md).

title: Bug: DROP_VECTOR_INDEX leaves corrupted metadata preventing property updates

code_snippets.code: Runtime exception: Cannot set property vec in table embeddings because it is used in one or more indexes. Try delete and then insert.

-- Step 1: Create a node table with vector property
CREATE NODE TABLE Person(id STRING, name STRING, embeddings FLOAT[128], PRIMARY KEY(id));

-- Step 2: Insert a test node
CREATE (p:Person {id: "person-1", name: "Alice", embeddings: [0.1, 0.2, 0.3, ..., 0.128]});

-- Step 3: Create vector index on embeddings property
CALL CREATE_VECTOR_INDEX(
    'Person',
    'person_embeddings_idx',
    'embeddings',
    mu := 30,
    ml := 60,
    pu := 0.05,
    metric := 'cosine',
    efc := 200,
    cache_embeddings := true
);

-- Step 4: Verify index was created
CALL SHOW_INDEXES() RETURN *;
-- Output: Shows person_embeddings_idx on Person.embeddings

-- Step 5: Drop the vector index
CALL DROP_VECTOR_INDEX('Person', 'person_embeddings_idx');
-- Output: "Table _X_person_embeddings_idx_LOWER has been dropped."

-- Step 6: Verify index was removed
CALL SHOW_INDEXES() RETURN *;
-- Output: Empty result (no indexes remain)

-- Step 7: Try to update the embeddings property
MATCH (p:Person {id: "person-1"})
SET p.embeddings = [0.2, 0.3, 0.4, ..., 0.129]
RETURN p.id;

-- ERROR: Runtime exception: Cannot set property vec in table embeddings because it is used in one or more indexes. Try delete and then insert.

-- Non-indexed properties on the same table work fine
MATCH (p:Person {id: "person-1"})
SET p.name = "Updated Name"
RETURN p.name;
-- Success!

title: Fix QueryResult iterator exhaustion bug in Rust bindings
body:
The toString() method in MaterializedQueryResult was incorrectly using the shared class member 'iterator' instead of the local 'iterator_' variable. This caused the shared iterator to be exhausted whenever toString() was called (e.g., when using Display trait in Rust).

This made the QueryResult unusable for iteration after any display/print operation, causing the iterator to hang or return no results.

Changed:
- iterator->hasNext() to iterator_.hasNext()
- iterator->getNext() to iterator_.getNext()

This ensures toString() uses its own local iterator without affecting the shared iterator used by the Rust bindings.

Fixes the issue where Rust QueryResult iterator would hang after Display.

title: Update workflow to use self-hosted runners for Mac ARM builds
Fix potential overflow when writing uncompressed data + fix dictionary offsets when scanning from string column
body:
# Description

This PR fixes the following issues

1. When writing uncompressed data we copy the entire buffer to disk instead of just copying the correct number of values based on `numValues`. Since the size of the buffer is based on capacity, this can result in writing past the end of the allocated page range and corrupting data.
2. When appending to the dictionary chunk, we used the number of strings in the initial result instead of the number of distinct strings (in other words the size of the dictionary chunk) as the base size.

body:
**Kuzu version v0.11.2, Ubuntu 24**

Create a **file** database (this does not happen in-memory). Then run:

```cypher
install json;
load json;
create node table frame(id serial primary key, cells map(string, json));
create (n:frame {cells: map([], [])});
checkpoint;
create (n:frame {cells: map(['a', 'b'], [json('{"row":1}'), json('{"row":2}')])});
checkpoint;
match (n:frame) return n.cells;
```
The output is:

```
┌───────────────────┐
```

whereas , if we run this in `:memory:`, the output is:

title: Bug: KU_UNREACHABLE Error when using .get_as_df() on a query with relationship property filters
body:
### Kuzu version

v0.11.2

### What operating system are you using?

Windows 11 Pro

### What happened?

When executing a Cypher query that filters on relationship properties (e.g., WHERE r.confidence_score < $threshold) and then attempting to convert the result to a Pandas DataFrame using .get_as_df(), Kùzu throws a RuntimeError with a KU_UNREACHABLE assertion failure.

The error suggests a bug within the internal C++ result-to-DataFrame converter, as the Kùzu developers believed the state leading to this error was impossible to reach. The query executes successfully, but the serialization to a DataFrame fails.

A manual iteration over the results using .get_next() works as expected, confirming the issue is specific to the .get_as_df() method for this type of query result

### Are there known steps to reproduce?

## Steps to Reproduce 
The following self-contained Python script reliably reproduces the error. It sets up a minimal graph, runs a query similar to the one causing the issue, and fails on the .get_as_df() call.

Python

import kuzu
import pandas as pd
import os
import shutil

DB_NAME = "repro_db"

## Clean up previous runs
if os.path.exists(DB_NAME):
    shutil.rmtree(DB_NAME)

## 1. Setup the database and schema
db = kuzu.Database(DB_NAME)
conn = kuzu.Connection(db)

print("--- Creating Schema ---")
conn.execute("CREATE NODE TABLE Entity(name STRING, PRIMARY KEY (name));")
conn.execute("""
    CREATE REL TABLE HasRelationship(
        FROM Entity TO Entity,
        confidence_score DOUBLE,
        status STRING
    );
""")

## 2. Insert minimal data to trigger the bug
print("--- Inserting Data ---")
conn.execute("CREATE (e:Entity {name: 'SubjectA'})")
conn.execute("CREATE (e:Entity {name: 'ObjectB'})")
conn.execute("""
    MATCH (a:Entity {name: 'SubjectA'}), (b:Entity {name: 'ObjectB'})
    CREATE (a)-[:HasRelationship {confidence_score: 0.5, status: 'unverified'}]->(b)
""")
print("Data inserted.")

## 3. The query and the line that causes the crash
query = """
    MATCH (a)-[r]->(b)
    WHERE r.confidence_score < $threshold AND r.status <> 'verified'
    RETURN a.name AS subject, label(r) AS relationship, b.name AS object,
           r.confidence_score AS score, id(r) AS rel_id
    LIMIT 10;
"""
params = {"threshold": 0.7}

print("\n--- Running Query ---")
try:
    weak_rels_result = conn.execute(query, params)
    
    print("Query executed successfully. Attempting to convert to DataFrame...")
    
    # THIS IS THE LINE THAT FAILS
    df = weak_rels_result.get_as_df() 
    
    print("Successfully created DataFrame:")
    print(df)

except RuntimeError as e:
    print(f"\n--- ERROR ---")
    print(f"Caught the expected RuntimeError: {e}")
    print("This confirms the bug in .get_as_df().")

Expected Behavior
The code should execute without error, and a Pandas DataFrame containing the query results should be printed to the console.

Actual Behavior
The script executes the query but fails during the DataFrame conversion, raising the following error:

RuntimeError: Assertion failed in file "[...]\py_query_result_converter.cpp" on line 185 
(my exact error was: RuntimeError: Assertion failed in file "C:\Users\runner\AppData\Local\Temp\cibw-sdist-m1tz62cu\sdist\kuzu-source\tools\python_api\src_cpp\py_query_result_converter.cpp" on line 185: KU_UNREACHABLE)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
**Workaround**
A reliable workaround is to bypass the .get_as_df() method and manually construct the list of dictionaries by iterating through the query result object. This proves the query itself is sound and the issue is isolated to the converter.


## --- WORKAROUND ---
--- This code replaces the failing 'weak_rels_result.get_as_df()' call. ---

print("\n--- Applying Workaround ---")
weak_rels_result = conn.execute(query, params) # Re-run query for demonstration

weak_rels = []
column_names = weak_rels_result.get_column_names()
while weak_rels_result.has_next():
    row_values = weak_rels_result.get_next()
    weak_rels.append(dict(zip(column_names, row_values)))

print("Successfully built results manually:")
print(pd.DataFrame(weak_rels))

title: Bug: Loss of data after CHECKPOINT with LIST of STRUCT
body:
### Kuzu version

v0.11.2

### What operating system are you using?

Ubuntu 24

### What happened?

A database with these contents:

```
INSTALL json;
LOAD json;
CREATE NODE TABLE TestNode (
    id STRING PRIMARY KEY,
    grids STRUCT(`type` STRING, `display` BOOL, `params` JSON)[],
);

CREATE (n:TestNode { `id`: 'test_0_0_0', `grids`: [] });
CREATE (n:TestNode { `id`: 'test_0_0_1', `grids`: [{ `type`: "column", `display`: true, `params`: to_json({color: {r: 0, g: 0, b: 1}}) }] });
CREATE (n:TestNode { `id`: 'test_1_1_0', `grids`: [{ `type`: "column", `display`: true, `params`: to_json({color: {r: 1, g: 1, b: 0}}) }] });
CREATE (n:TestNode { `id`: 'test_1_1_1', `grids`: [] });
```

stores corrupted (empty) "grids" fields when:

1. Constructed with the python API
2. Using disk storage, i.e. not using ":memory:"
3. Checkpointing after every CREATE

### Are there known steps to reproduce?

Note that the issue does not appear when evaluating cypher on the kuzu repl.

Here's [a python script to reproduce](https://gist.github.com/mdbenito/8fc5a3d40337fcf3fa8aac8807486d67). The script creates the database, then adds nodes one by one and calls `checkpoint` after each insertion.

Below is some of the relevant output from that script (the "data after insert" refers only to the `grids` field):

```
✓ Inserted test_0_0_0
```

body:
### Kuzu version

### What operating system are you using?

Ubuntu 20.04, PowerPC8

### What happened?

Kuzu fails on PowerPC64LE (ppc64le) architecture with buffer manager exceptions during database operations. The error occurs in both C++ and Node.js interfaces:  
                                                                                                                                                          
  **_Buffer manager exception: Releasing physical memory associated with a frame failed with error code -1: Invalid argument.**_                                                  
 
 What I expected:
Normal database operations and test execution, similar to x86_64 platforms.                                                               

System Information:

Architecture: PowerPC64LE (ppc64le)
OS: Ubuntu 20.04.1 LTS
Kuzu versions tested: v0.10.1 and v0.11.1
Node.js: v22.19.0
Hardware: PowerPC8

### Are there known steps to reproduce?

Build Kuzu on PowerPC64LE system: make release NUM_THREADS=$(nproc)
make test NUM_THREADS=$(nproc)                                                                                                                              Build Node.js bindings: make nodejs NUM_THREADS=$(nproc)
Run Node.js tests: make nodejstest NUM_THREADS=$(nproc)
Error occurs during database initialization in test suite

title: Optimize checkpointing updates
body:
# Description

This PR changes the checkpointing of updates so that segments are only scanned + rewritten if updates are applied to them. Previously, this happened at the column chunk level.

This is done by introducing a `ColumnChunkScanner` interface which is used by `ColumnChunk::scanCommitted()` and determines which `ChunkCheckpointStates` to write out. A `LazySegmentScanner` implementation of the interface is then used when scanning + writing updates.

For normal node groups, the `ChunkCheckpointStates` to write mirror the structure (start row, num rows) of the existing segments on disk. However, for CSR node groups we use a different strategy. Here, we skip writing to rows if we can (generally when old/new CSR offsets for an unchanged value are the same) and each new `ChunkCheckpointState` is just a contiguous block of rows that we actually write to. It's then up to `ColumnChunk::checkpoint()` to split these into segments.

### Quick microbenchmark

Configuration: AMD Zen 3 CPU, `max_num_threads=10` (although checkpoint is single-threaded so shouldn't affect execution time by much)

**Node Group Checkpoint:**

Dataset: ldbc-sf100 Comment (first 39060410 rows)

Query:
Config: `auto_checkpoint=true`, `checkpoint_threshold=0`
```sql
match (c:comment) where offset(id(c)) % pow(2, 19) = 0 set c.content = concat(c.content, 'a') return c.id, c.content order by c.id
```

branch|execution time
----|----
master|30s
new|5s

**CSR Node Group Checkpoint:**

Dataset: ldbc-sf100 Comment (first 39060410 rows) + custom rel table (10M rows):

```sql
create rel table replyOf_Comment (FROM Comment TO Comment, str STRING);
copy replyOf_Comment from (match (c:comment) where c.id <> 39582418599937 and offset(id(c)) < 10000000 return 39582418599937, c.id, c.content)
```

Query:
Config: `auto_checkpoint=true`, `checkpoint_threshold=0`
```sql
match (:comment)-[r:replyOf_Comment]->(:comment) where offset(id(r)) % pow(2, 19) = 0 set r.str = concat(r.str, 'a') return r.str order by r.str
```

branch|execution time (1st time running query)|execution time (2nd time running query)
----|----|----
master|8.6s|7.9s
new|2.7s|2.4s

~~The reason why there is no performance improvement the 1st time we run the query (which is the first time we checkpoint after the COPY) is that currently we do not calculate in-memory stats when performing COPY (at least in some cases). During the 1st checkpoint, this causes us the underestimate the sizes of string segments (not sure about other segments) which results in us under-splitting which undermines the benefits of this optimization. It looks like after the 1st checkpoint, the in-memory statistics are accurate (enough?) and thus we can see the benefits of this optimization.~~

~~Since the fix for this is unrelated to this PR and the benefits of this PR are still visible through 2+ checkpoints, I won't consider that an issue here.~~

# Contributor agreement

- [ ] I have read and agree to the [Contributor Agreement](https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/blob/master/CLA.md).

title: Bug: Unbounded memory growth when LOAD-ing from Pandas dataframes

labels.name: type: perf bug
labels.description: Issues related to a regression in the performance

body:
### Kuzu version

v0.11.2

### What operating system are you using?

Ubuntu 24.04

### What happened?

This was also tested on MacOS Sequoia 15.6.

I am filling a graph from an index in Elasticsearch where documents are streamed from Elasticsearch, dataframes are created in small batches of ~100 documents, and then LOAD-ed into the graph. After LOAD/MERGE operations are finished the dataframes are cleared, repeating this process for the next batch.

After only 5-6 batches of ~100 documents/batch, the memory has grown to ~16GB and the process needs to be manually killed.

There is also a vector index, where some nodes have text embedding vectors with 128 dimensions, and other nodes have low-dimensional vectors from a pre-trained node2vec model. I am expecting ~5M nodes and 10-20M edges in the final graph, but the memory is exceeded well before that.

Naive profiling was done with `tracemalloc` to check the Python layer, but it doesn't look like the memory growth is happening at the scripting level.

There are a few LOAD statements of the variety
```cypher
LOAD FROM $df
MATCH (o:A {a_id: a_id}), (g:B {b_id: b_id})
CREATE (o)-[:REL]->(g);
```
but `a_id` and `b_id` are both PRIMARY KEY string index fields, so I would expect that `MATCH` statement to be performant. Also the dataframe being passed to `$df` only has 2 columns (`a_id`, `b_id`) for these id fields.

This was also tested on v0.11.1, but the same behavior was observed.

**Update**: I should have mentioned, but this is an on-disk database.

### Are there known steps to reproduce?

This is a simplified version of the issue:

```python
from uuid import uuid4
import pandas as pd
import kuzu


def initialize(conn: kuzu.Connection):
    conn.execute("INSTALL vector; LOAD vector;")
    conn.execute("CREATE NODE TABLE A(a_id STRING PRIMARY KEY, vector FLOAT[128]);")
    conn.execute("CREATE NODE TABLE B(b_id STRING PRIMARY KEY, vector FLOAT[16]);")
    conn.execute("CREATE REL TABLE AtoB(FROM A TO B);")


def insert(conn: kuzu.Connection, nodes_a: pd.DataFrame, nodes_b: pd.DataFrame, relations: pd.DataFrame):
    conn.execute(
        query="COPY A FROM $df;",
        parameters={"df": nodes_a}
    )

    conn.execute(
        query="COPY B FROM $df;",
        parameters={"df": nodes_b}
    )

    conn.execute(
        query="""
        LOAD FROM $df
        MATCH (a:A {a_id: a_id}), (b:B {b_id: b_id})
        CREATE (a)-[:AtoB]->(b);
        """,
        parameters={"df": relations}
    )


def data_gen():
    a = [{"a_id": uuid4().hex, "vector": [0.1] * 128} for _ in range(100)]
    b = [{"b_id": uuid4().hex, "vector": [0.1] * 16} for _ in range(10)]

    rel = []
    for i in range(len(a)):
        for j in range(len(b)):
            rel.append({"a_id": a[i]["a_id"], "b_id": b[j]["b_id"]})
    return pd.DataFrame(a), pd.DataFrame(b), pd.DataFrame(rel)


db = kuzu.Database("temp.kuzu")

with kuzu.Connection(db) as c:
    initialize(c)

for _ in range(100):
    _a, _b, _r = data_gen()
    with kuzu.Connection(db) as c:
        insert(conn=c, nodes_a=_a, nodes_b=_b, relations=_r)
```

title: Feature: native support for synonyms in FTS
body:
FTS is already great since advanced features like stopwords and stemming for several languages are available.

What is missing, is the possibility to natively deal with synonyms.
Of course using vector search works in this direction, but its not the same.
Sometimes e.g. for pre-filtering the graph, one prefer relying on exact matches.

typical usecases:

1. abbreviations:
CFRP <-> Carbon Fiber Reinforced Plastic

2. common foreign language usage in special domains
Lion <-> Panthera leo

3. name variants:
Robert <-> Bob


If one would like to directly start with design decisions being prepared for further advancements, there are some things to consider:
- synonyms may consists of several words (see given examples)
- may work uni- and bi-directional (syntax driven)
- do one need a transparent/hinted separation of exact matches (original word) and synonyms?
- one should care for interacting with wild card pattern matching/advanced_pattern_match https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/pull/5998
- one should care for interacting with stemming
- there may be more than one synonym for a word/phrase
- each synonym may have a weight (to be able to boost the ones that are closer to the original concept/more important for current domain)
- one may have a look at lucene's functionality and syntax
```
leopard, big cat|0.8, bagheera|0.9, panthera pardus|0.85
lion => panthera leo|0.9, simba leo|0.8, kimba|0.75
```

lion => panthera leo|0.9, simba leo|0.8, kimba|0.75

title: Feature: Support multiple FROM and TO pairs when copying into REL tables
body:
Currently, `COPY SomeRelation FROM ...` fails if `SomeRelation` contains multiple connections. This makes it hard to import data in bulk in these cases.

Something like this:

```cypher
CREATE REL TABLE LivesWith(FROM Person TO Pet, FROM Person TO Person);
COPY LivesWith FROM 'lives_with.csv' (header=true);
```

fails with:

```
Error: Binder exception: The table LivesWith has multiple FROM and TO pairs defined in the schema. A specific pair of FROM and TO options is expected when copying data into the LivesWith table.
```

It would be nice to be able to do something like:

```cypher
COPY LivesWith(FROM Person TO Pet) FROM 'lives_with.csv' (header=true);
```

COPY LivesWith FROM 'lives_with.csv' (header=true);

This may be 2 separate bugs, but are closely related to each other, since they both make csv exports not function as expected

2. The generated `copy.cypher` file has errors which makes it not importable. The `quote`, `delim`, & `escape` arguments are duplicated like

title: Bug: The C API for BLOBs is not really usable.
body:
### Kuzu version

V0.11.*

### What operating system are you using?

Fedora 41

### What happened?

`kuzu_value_get_blob` says: "Returns the blob value of the given value. The returned buffer is null-terminated similar
to a string."

This is not at all useful for BLOBS, because it relies on the caller using `strlen` to determine the length of the blob, and assumes there are no null (zero) bytes in the blob content.   Binary data has null bytes. 

Most of the tests and example cases simply show four non-zero bytes being stuffed in a blob then retrieved (including the GO API), so they pretty much just propagate this flawed API.

The API should be revised at least minimally to return bytes and length as separate calls or values, and the misleading null byte should be eliminated.

While we're here, the online documentation for the BLOB [data type](https://docs.kuzudb.com/cypher/data-types/#blob) says that BLOBs are limited to 4k bytes.  xiyangf says he believes this was changed in 2021 in this Discord thread: https://discord.com/channels/1196510116388806837/1196510116871159909/1411378772346933379

If BLOBs are really just 4k bytes, I would voice an opinion that t hey are not very useful, but it may be I just don't understand the Kuzudb use case.  If they actually have very large size capabilities, then a new/fixed blob API should probably have some way to stream or manipulate them in chunks.

### Are there known steps to reproduce?

_No response_

title: Bug: UUIDs/int128_t can cause compression to fail during checkpointing
body:
### Kuzu version

master

### What operating system are you using?

_No response_

### What happened?

This is a very edge case. For UUIDs, it should eventually be fixed by https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/5577 (when we change UUIDs to use `uint128_t` internally) but for `int128_t` this is still a problem.

We currently store UUIDs as `int128_t`. This can be a problem as it is not possible to negate `INT128_MIN`, and during compression we take the `abs` of the value we wish to compress in `IntegerBitpacking<T>::getPackingInfo()`.

Currently, negating `INT128_MIN` will throw an exception which will cause compression (and thus checkpointing) to fail which is undesirable. We might want to make this behaviour less restrictive and avoid throwing an exception in this case but we need to first confirm that compression will still work as expected in this case.

title: Feature: Support updating nodes with a vector index

labels.name: type: feature
labels.description: New features or missing components of existing features

body:
### API

Other

### Description

It looks like this is a known limitation from the error message, but I was curious if there are any plans to support updates of nodes with a vector index.

Example setup:
```
install vector;
load vector;

create node table Text (id uint64 primary key, content string, embedding float[3]);
call create_vector_index('Text', 'TextEmbedding', 'embedding');
create (:Text {id: 1, content: "one", embedding: [1,2,3]});
create (:Text {id: 2, content: "two"});
```

Then either of these updates:
```
match (x:Text) where x.id = 1 set x.embedding = [4,5,6] return x;
```
or
```
match (x:Text) where x.id = 2 set x.embedding = [4,5,6] return x;
```
returns this error:
```
Error: Runtime exception: Cannot set property vec in table embeddings because it is used in one or more indexes. Try delete and then insert.
```

The suggested solution ("Try delete and then insert.") will be difficult as the update would occur after this `Text` node has been linked via relations to other nodes.

My use case in this example would be to initially import the text (and its relations to other nodes) immediately and then back-fill the text embedding vector later.

I currently work around it by delaying creation of the index itself, but it would be nice to not have to re-create the entire index after every batch update.

Thanks!

match (x:Text) where x.id = 2 set x.embedding = [4,5,6] return x;
Error: Runtime exception: Cannot set property vec in table embeddings because it is used in one or more indexes. Try delete and then insert.

title: Segmentation
body:
This is just the initial segmentation implementation; there is more work to be done which will be done in follow-up PRs. 

ColumnChunks are now segmented so that they generally do not exceed 256KB, storing a list of `ColumnChunkData` instead of just one both in-memory and on-disk (there are now separate `ColumnChunkMetadata` and `SegmentMetadata`). Currently nested types are nested inside each segment, but eventually nested types should be split up so that they are segmented individually (e.g. in this implementation each struct segment has a child segment for each field, but eventually structs chunks should have a collection of segments for each field).

The `ChunkedNodeGroup` was split into `InMemChunkedNodeGroup` (storing a `ColumnChunkData` and ChunkedNodeGroup (storing a `ColumnChunk`) since the temporary chunks used during copying needed functions which I wasn't initially sure how to implement for a collection of ColumnChunkData. They will probably be merged back together when segmentation for copies is refactored to occur during the copy instead of after the copy. 

Future PRs
- Rel table checkpointing isn't doing segmentation in one of the code paths (started, and never finished, but it's just for non-copy checkpoints inserting into a new column chunk, which would rarely need multiple segments).
- [x] Certain string scans are currently very inefficient (scanning the entire dictionary instead of just the requested values) (might include this in this PR depending on how long it takes, I have it implemented, but for some reason it's not working; it may be related to one of the failing in-memory tests).
- I have omitted renaming `ColumnChunkData` to `Segment` since this PR is already very large and I think it would be better to do that in a follow-up PR that only makes that change.
- Segmentation should happen during a copy instead of splitting afterwards (part of the issue is that calculating the on-disk size of a segment is currently inefficient; we need to fully track the in-memory statistics (which are currently just used by the functions needed for in-place updates I think) and then should be able to detect the on-disk size in constant time (per nested chunk at least) instead of having to scan the chunk each time.
- Refactoring nested segmentation (struct is probably easiest, then list/null; strings are more complicated due to dictionary compression) 
- Reading segments as a unit (will require a change to the buffer manager): this will make it possible to simplify ALP compression so that it can store everything in one segment, and something similar could be done for strings/dictionary compression.

## Benchmarks
As of e2e336d01971cf182a7734b220d0773e8240e38c
I made a small optimization to the split function. Performance is generally quite similar to the original, but there is a noticeable additional cost when splitting strings (maybe other nested types too, but strings are particularly bad because of dictionary compression maintaining a hash set of strings). The planned change to create segments of the desired size as we copy should bring performance in line with the current master version.

| Query | Master | Segmentation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy 100M integers into node table | 12.4s | 12.5s |
| Copy 100M short strings into node table | 16.2s | 19.0s |
| Copy 141593190 edges from the datagen-9_0-fb dataset | 26.7s | 27.1s |

title: Checksum WAL records
body:
# Description

Add checksums to each individual record of the WAL, which we check against when replaying the WAL. This is done by making WAL reads/writes go through the new classes `ChecksumReader/Writer`. The functions `startEntry()`/`finishEntry()` are called before/after processing a WAL record, after which a buffer containing the accumulated serialized record in the reader/writer will be used to calculate the checksum.

## Performance

I also did a quick microbenchmark to get a feel for the performance impact of adding the checksum on replaying a transaction.

**Transaction:**

```
with kuzu.Database(tempdir + "/db.kz") as db, kuzu.Connection(db) as conn:
        conn.execute("call force_checkpoint_on_close=false")
        conn.execute("call auto_checkpoint=false")
        conn.execute("begin transaction")
        conn.execute("create node table nodes(id int64 primary key)")
        conn.execute("create rel table edges(from nodes to nodes)")

        NUM_NODES = 1000000
        conn.execute(f"unwind range(1, {NUM_NODES}) as i create (nodes{{id: i}})")
        conn.execute("commit")
```

|Branch|Average transaction execution time|Average replay time|
|--|--|--|
master|2.87s|2.40s
new|2.95s|2.54s

Average replay time on master: 1.23s
Average replay time on new branch: 1.34s

C

The C API is missing array retrieval functions, and incorrectly documents kuzu_value_get_list_size as requiring an array, when it only works for list types.

title: Merge free pages after rollback
body:
Previously only happened during a checkpoint.
But if a rollback occurs after data has been written, there would be a bunch of small page ranges in the free page cache from data appended to the end of the file, which can be merged and truncated.

This works around an issue I was running into on my segmentation branch (`CopyNodeAfterPKErrorRollbackFlushedGroups`; maybe related to the issue with `NODE_GROUP_SIZE_LOG2=12` in the FIXME, but I couldn't reproduce that), so I suspect that might be related to free space management (which probably hits this edge case by segmentation increasing the number of data chunks we're dealing with). I don't think it fixes that issue though.

### What happened?

I am currently writing an api wrapper for Kotlin Multiplatform to wrap existing api's into a multiplatform library. Currently, the only api implemented is the Java API.         }
```kotlin
    }
```

title: Graceful handling of stray WAL/shadow files
body:
# Description

Fixes https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/5777

Introduces the a database ID to the database header which is used to uniquely identify kuzu databases.

For WAL and shadow files, we write the database ID to the header of the file. We then check the IDs before replaying to make sure that it matches the ID of the data.kz file. If they do not match, an exception is thrown. This helps gracefully deal with the case where stray WAL/shadow files are left (e.g. after closing a Jupyter notebook) before a database file is deleted and prevents the files from erroneously being replayed when creating a new database with the same name.

We avoid doing the same for other temporary files (like the spiller files) as they are not expected to persist after a database is killed and will be deleted if they do persist.

Docs PR: https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu-docs/pull/632

title: Feature: initial GraphAr storage-format extension for Kuzu
body:
### API

C++

### Description

**TL;DR**

A minimal, first-cut GraphAr extension for Kuzu has been implemented (uses GraphAr + Arrow C++ SDKs for simplicity). The demo recognizes GraphAr YAML schema and parallel-reads data, converting it into Kuzu’s internal node/edge structures so the format can be consumed via `LOAD` / `COPY` workflows. 

**Context**

GraphAr ([[Apache incubating](https://graphar.apache.org/)](https://graphar.apache.org/)) is a property-graph storage format designed to facilitate efficient exchange and interoperability of graph data across systems.  It exposes YAML metadata and stores data with Arrow, Parquet, and other columnar formats.  Intended to serve as a standard file format for importing/exporting and persistent storage of graph data, GraphAr reduces the overhead when diverse systems need to co-work.  To make Kuzu able to read and write GraphAr datasets, I implemented a extension that (1) parses GraphAr schema, (2) maps GraphAr columns to Kuzu types, (3) parallel-loads data into Kuzu internal representations using the Arrow reader interfaces.

**Implementation (first draft)**

Repository branch: https://github.com/gary-cloud/kuzu/tree/graphar-extension

**Notes on design choices**

- Keep the core Kuzu code untouched where possible; the feature lives as an extension layer that translates GraphAr → Kuzu types.
- Reuse GraphAr and Arrow C++ SDKs to avoid reimplementing low-level IO and schema logic.
- Demo implements parallel chunk readers that convert record batches into Kuzu insert streams.

**Usage examples**

```
 LOAD FROM ".../ldbc_sample.graph.yml" (file_format="graphar", table_name="person") RETURN *;
 CREATE NODE TABLE Person(id INT64, firstName STRING, lastName STRING, gender STRING, PRIMARY KEY (id));
 COPY Person FROM ".../ldbc_sample.graph.yml" (file_format="graphar", table_name="person");
```

**Expected outcome**

- Users can `LOAD` or `COPY` GraphAr datasets into Kuzu without manual pre-conversion.
- The extension demonstrates a concrete approach for future third-party storage-format integrations.

### **Request for Kuzu team feedback**

I’d like the Kuzu maintainers’ high-level opinion on this approach and whether this extension should move into the core repo, remain as an external contrib, or be refactored to follow an official extension API (if one exists/planned). General feedback on integration approach, testing expectations, and project placement would be appreciated.

### **Related / corresponding issues**

- GraphAr: https://github.com/apache/incubator-graphar/issues/679
- Kuzu: https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/5795

CC: @SemyonSinchenko (GraphAr) — please feel free to weigh in on format mapping and any GraphAr-specific compatibility concerns. 

Thanks in advance for any guidance!

title: Add loop and set random in testing framework
body:
# Description

Added the support for `LOOP` and `random` in the testing framework, which can be used to simulate random workloads with a fixed or dynamic seed more easily.
`LOOP` is intended to take in:
 - `<start> <end> [step]`
 - `<[list of values]>`

Only `randInt64` is added for now, which can be expanded to support `randStr` and more types. The best way is actually to remove `random` from the testing framework, but use Cypher functions, which we do not support right now.

After this, the `create_random_int.test` is rewritten in a much easier way as following.

```
-CASE TSSeedRandomInt64Insertions
-SKIP_WASM
-STATEMENT CREATE NODE TABLE test(id SERIAL, prop INT64, PRIMARY KEY(id));
---- ok
-SET seed current_timestamp()
-LOG seed: ${seed}
-SET _ random.set_seed(${seed})
-LOOP i 1 1000
-SET val random.randInt64(1000000)
-STATEMENT CREATE (t:test {prop: ${val}});
---- ok
-ENDLOOP
-STATEMENT MATCH (t:test) RETURN COUNT(*);
---- 1
1000

-CASE FixedSeedRandomInt64Insertions
-SKIP_WASM
-STATEMENT CREATE NODE TABLE test(id SERIAL, prop INT64, PRIMARY KEY(id));
---- ok
-SET seed 1234567890
-LOG seed: ${seed}
-SET _ random.set_seed(${seed})
-LOOP i 1 1000
-SET val random.randInt64(1000000)
-STATEMENT CREATE (t:test {prop: ${val}});
---- ok
-ENDLOOP
-STATEMENT MATCH (t:test) RETURN COUNT(*);
---- 1
1000
-STATEMENT MATCH (t:test) RETURN sum(t.prop);
---- 1
502790265
```

The PR also reworks a bit how test statements are parsed to make it more readable, though more refactoring is needed later to make it more robust.

title: Bug: Segmentation fault in finalizers when garbage collection is triggered
body:
### Kuzu version

v0.11.0

### What operating system are you using?

MacOS Sequoia 15

### What happened?

  ### Summary
  Kuzu crashes with segmentation fault when JavaScript garbage collection triggers native finalizers. This prevents usage in JavaScript runtimes that properly implement N-API finalizer calls.

  ### Environment
  - **Kuzu Version**: 0.11.1
  - **Node.js Version**: 22.12.0
  - **Platform**: macOS Darwin 24.4.0
  - **Also reproduced on**: Linux, with Bun 1.2.20

  ### Reproduction
  This issue can be reproduced by creating multiple Kuzu database instances and then forcing garbage collection:

  ```bash
  # Install dependencies
  npm install kuzu tsx

  # Run reproduction script
  node --expose-gc --import tsx/esm kuzu-finalizer-bug-repro.ts

  Minimal reproduction code:
  import kuzu from 'kuzu';

  async function reproduce() {
    // Create multiple database instances
    for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
      const db = new kuzu.Database(`./test-${i}.db`);
      const conn = new kuzu.Connection(db);
      await conn.init();
      await conn.query('CREATE NODE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS Test(id STRING, PRIMARY KEY(id))');
      await conn.close();
      await db.close();
    }

    // Force garbage collection - this triggers the crash
    if (global.gc) {
      global.gc(); // Segmentation fault occurs here
    }
  }
```

  ### Expected Behavior

  Objects should be cleanly garbage collected without crashes.

  ### Actual Behavior

  Segmentation fault occurs when finalizers are called during garbage collection.

  ### Error Details

  Segmentation fault: 11
  panic(main thread): Segmentation fault at address 0x8

  ### Impact

  - Blocks production deployment in Bun runtime (which properly calls finalizers)
  - Potential memory leaks in Node.js (which rarely calls finalizers)
  - Affects any multi-database application

  ### Analysis

  This appears to be a bug in Kuzu's N-API finalizer implementation, possibly:
  - Use-after-free in cleanup code
  - Double-free of native resources
  - Missing null checks in finalizers
  - Improper cleanup ordering

  ### Runtime Behavior Differences

  - Bun: Crashes during normal operation (calls finalizers properly)
  - Node.js: Usually works (rarely calls finalizers) but crashes when forced with --expose-gc

  This suggests the bug is in Kuzu's finalizer code, not the JavaScript runtimes.

  ### Files

  I have a complete reproduction case available if needed for debugging. (mcl0vinit/bun-kuzu-segfault-repro)

title: fix(python): add support for bytes parameters in BLOB fields
body:
## Problem

The Python API was failing with `AttributeError: module 'importlib' has no attribute 'util'` when passing Python `bytes` objects directly as parameters for BLOB fields.

**Expected behavior:** Python `bytes` should be accepted directly for BLOB parameters since BLOB stands for Binary Large Object.

**Previously:** Users had to manually convert bytes to hex strings and use the `BLOB()` function.

## Solution

This PR adds support for Python `bytes` objects in BLOB contexts across the Python API.

### Changes Made

- **Type detection**: Add recognition for Python `bytes` objects as BLOB type
- **Parameter handling**: Convert `bytes` to BLOB when used as query parameters
- **Data ingestion**: Support `bytes` objects when loading data from Python
- **UDF support**: Allow `bytes` as input/output types in user-defined functions

### Implementation Details

- Fixes the `Python bytes → Kuzu BLOB` conversion using Python C API (`PyBytes_AsString`, `PyBytes_Size`) 
- The reverse direction `Kuzu BLOB → Python bytes` (query results) was already working correctly
- Maintains full round-trip consistency: `Python bytes → Kuzu BLOB → Python bytes`
- Preserves backward compatibility with existing `BLOB("\\xHH")` syntax

### Test Coverage

Test suite (`test_blob_parameter.py`) covers:
- ✅ Basic bytes parameters (raw binary, text, large data, empty, null)
- ✅ UTF-8 end-to-end conversion
- ✅ Backward compatibility with string + `BLOB()`
- ✅ CRUD operations (CREATE, UPDATE, WHERE clauses)
- ✅ Mixed parameter types
- ✅ Relationship properties with BLOB
- ✅ User-defined functions with bytes
- ✅ Error handling for invalid types

Fixes #5859

# Contributor agreement

```
CREATE NODE TABLE test (pk SERIAL, m MAP(INT, STRUCT(m STRING, x DOUBLE[2])), PRIMARY KEY(pk));

CREATE (n:test {m: map([1],[{m: "brr", x: [1.0, 2.0] }])});

EXPORT DATABASE 'test.db';
```

Then:

```
kuzu> IMPORT DATABASE ‘test.db;’

Error: Runtime exception: Import database failed: Conversion exception: Unsupported casting function from STRUCT(key INT32, value STRUCT(m STRING, x DOUBLE[])) to STRUCT(KEY INT32, VALUE STRUCT(m STRING, x DOUBLE[2])).
```

This does **not** happen if the STRUCT is not nested inside a MAP

code_snippets.code:
kuzu> IMPORT DATABASE ‘test.db;’

Error: Runtime exception: Import database failed: Conversion exception: Unsupported casting function from STRUCT(key INT32, value STRUCT(m STRING, x DOUBLE[])) to STRUCT(KEY INT32, VALUE STRUCT(m STRING, x DOUBLE[2])).

title: Bug: Inconsistent BLOB parameter handling in Python API
body:
### Kuzu version

v0.11.1

### What operating system are you using?

Debian Testing (trixie, 13)

### What happened?

The Python API has problematic BLOB parameter handling that corrupts data or requires kludgy workarounds:

**Primary issue**: Cannot pass Python bytes objects directly as BLOB parameters. Attempting to do so results in `AttributeError: module 'importlib' has no attribute 'util'`.

**Data corruption with standard approach**: Using the standard `bytes.hex()` method with `BLOB()` function results in data corruption. A 32-byte binary hash becomes 64 bytes (or 34 and 66 with '0x' appended), where each hexadecimal character is stored as an individual byte rather than being interpreted as hexadecimal data.

**Working solution**: The method that preserves data integrity is using a kludgy string manipulation: `''.join(f'\\x{b:02x}' for b in binary)` combined with the `BLOB()` function. This hack produces the correct 32-byte result but is unintuitive.

**API asymmetry**: While Kuzu correctly returns BLOB fields as Python bytes objects, it cannot accept bytes objects as input parameters, breaking expected API symmetry.

**Expected behavior:** 
- Accept Python bytes objects directly as BLOB parameters (or automatically handle hex strings) without requiring the `BLOB()` function.
- Maintain data integrity: input 32 bytes → store 32 bytes → retrieve 32 bytes.
- Handle `binary.hex()` + `BLOB()` correctly without data corruption (even if it is necessary to add “0x”)

Tested on Python versions 3.13 and 3.11

### Are there known steps to reproduce?

```python
import kuzu
import hashlib

db = kuzu.Database(":memory:")
conn = kuzu.Connection(db)
conn.execute("CREATE NODE TABLE Test(name STRING PRIMARY KEY, bin BLOB)")

binary = hashlib.sha256(b"testing").digest()
print(f"Original: {binary}")
print(f"Length: {len(binary)} bytes")
# Original: b"\xcf\x80\xcd\x8a\xedH-]\x15'\xd7\xdcr\xfc\xef\xf8Nc&Y(HD}-\xc0\xb0\xe8}\xfc\x9a\x90"
# Length: 32 bytes


# ⛔ Fails - cannot pass bytes directly
try:
    data = {"name": "test0", "bin": binary}
    conn.execute("CREATE (t:Test {name: $name, bin: $bin})", data)
except AttributeError as e:
    print(f"Error: {e}")  # Error: module 'importlib' has no attribute 'util'


# ⛔ Fails - misinterpreted
data = {"name": "test1", "bin": binary.hex()}  # ⚠️
conn.execute("CREATE (t:Test {name: $name, bin: BLOB($bin)})", data)


# ⛔ Fails - misinterpreted
data = {"name": "test2", "bin": "0x" + binary.hex()}  # ⚠️
conn.execute("CREATE (t:Test {name: $name, bin: BLOB($bin)})", data)


# ✅ Workaround: string manipulation hack and BLOB function use
chars = ''.join(f'\\x{b:02x}' for b in binary)  # ⚠️
data = {"name": "test3", "bin": chars}
conn.execute("CREATE (t:Test {name: $name, bin: BLOB($bin)})", data)


# 📋 Queries and results
ret = conn.execute("MATCH (a:Test) RETURN a.name, a.bin")
results = ret.get_all()
for name, blob in results:
    print(f"{name}: {type(blob)}, {len(blob)} bytes, {blob}")
# test1: <class 'bytes'>, 64 bytes, b'cf80cd8aed482d5d1527d7dc72fceff84e6326592848447d2dc0b0e87dfc9a90'
# test2: <class 'bytes'>, 66 bytes, b'0xcf80cd8aed482d5d1527d7dc72fceff84e6326592848447d2dc0b0e87dfc9a90'
# test3: <class 'bytes'>, 32 bytes, b"\xcf\x80\xcd\x8a\xedH-]\x15'\xd7\xdcr\xfc\xef\xf8Nc&Y(HD}-\xc0\xb0\xe8}\xfc\x9a\x90"
```

title: Proper error when cast invalid json
Rework UpdateInfo for concurrent updates
body:
# Description

We use `UpdateInfo` to track multiple versions of data if any were updated. 

Previously, the `UpdateInfo` wasn't designed for concurrent accesses, this PR adds proper locks within UpdateInfo for concurrent accesses. For each vector of data, a `UpdateNode` is kept as the head of the version list.
The locks are placed at two levels, one for the whole `UpdateInfo` structure, and one for each version list, i.e., `UpdateNode`.

The scan of update data is reworked as well, as there can be multiple transactions ongoing concurrently now. Previously we assume that only one writer exists, and the version chain should contain committed updates only (roll backed ones gets removed from the chain immediately). The scan now performs first by scanning the base data, then traversing the version chain and find the latest available update for each row and overwrite the scanned base data accordingly.

Note that the garbage collection is not done within this PR, which will come in a later one, as some further rework is needed separately.

A simple benchmark was performed locally on Mac mini with M4 pro chip. The benchmark is to update each tuple of a node table with 1M tuples with 1/2/4/8 threads under *in-memory mode*. Each update itself is a transaction. Each thread simply updates a sequential range of nodes to set an int64 property value to a new one.

The benchmark result:
| # threads | branch | time (ms) |
| --------- | ------- | ---------- |
| 1 | master | 106825 |
| 1 | new | 105715 |
| 2 | new | 64242 | 
| 4 | new | 44582 | 
| 8 | new | 33626 |

`F_FULLFSYNC` is required on MacOS/iOS to guarantee that the drive flushes its cache to disk. Also I added `fdatasync` which should be slightly faster than `fsync` is available to avoid full metadata sync.

Also, fixed file flags for `fsync` in WALReplay, and `fsync` should only happen when the database is opened in read-write mode.

title: Optimization: adopt rapidhash over murmur
body:
### Description

According to [smhasher's benchmarking of hash functions](https://rurban.github.io/smhasher/doc/table.html), murmur hashes at ~6GiB/s, and wyhash/rapidhash does ~22GiB/s.  Most of the hashing in kuzu looks like it's mostly to get a good distribution for 8 byte values, and a real quick benchmark I threw together seems to confirm that rapidhash is slightly faster even for 8byte values (as measured on my laptop):

```
------------------------------------------------------------
Benchmark                  Time             CPU   Iterations
------------------------------------------------------------
BM_murmur               1.93 ns         1.93 ns    362891921
BM_rapidhash            1.82 ns         1.81 ns    385887588
BM_rapidhashMicro       1.81 ns         1.81 ns    386442455
BM_rapidhashNano        1.82 ns         1.81 ns    387363102
```

It's also the choice of Folly's F14 hashtable, and I had spotchecked what [Dandelion Hash Tables](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2406.09986v1) used, to which they comment:
> We benchmarked many of the most prominent hash functions, including CityHash, xxHash, Murmur3, and FNV1. We found that wyhash provides the most favorable trade-off between performance and randomness.

And rapidhash is an improved wyhash.  Furthermore, [a study of mixing quality](https://github.com/martinus/better-faster-stronger-mixer) saw wyhash be orders of magnitude better at producing random-looking results out of a linearly evolving counter than murmur.

So, overall, it seems like a pretty reasonable choice to move to.  (Which if no one objects, I'll be slowly working on.)

labels.description: Issues related to better usability experience, including bad error messages

body:
### API

C

### Description

While building lisp API support based on the C API, I noticed that the semantics of `kuzu_prepared_statement_bind_timestamp_tz` and `kuzu_prepared_statement_bind_timestamp` appear to be identical.  The comments on their respective structs https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/blob/master/src/include/c_api/kuzu.h#L246-L258 indicate that they both accept microsecond deltas from the epoch.   Perhaps the tz variant was originally meant to do more, but it seems to interpret the microsecond value as UTC based just like vanilla 'timestamp' interfaces do.

In a discussion with Guodong Jin in Discord he indicated that he spoke with the team that it is probably reasonable to deprecate the timestamp_tz materials.  If it is somehow doing more with timezones, then more documentation should be added to describe how the timezone context is provided and used, but that doesn't seem to be the case at this time.

title: Cache prepared statement in client context
body:
# Description

As we develop the server, prepare can no longer work as in the embedded case, e.g. we cannot/ there is no obvious benefit to serialize logical plan and send back to client side for parameter binding. This PR adds `CachedPrepareStatement` to store state that is always maintained on the server side. 

The current prepare workflow is

1. Prepare a logical plan and store in client context. Return back a string based identifier to user.
2. When executing, use string identifier to retain prepared state and rebind/execute.

We will probably need a few more iteration on this change.

title: fsync() the WAL on open
body:
# Description

It's generally wise to ensure that whatever set of changes are being recovered from the WAL are actually durable before they're processed. By a strict interpretation of the UNIX spec, the fsync() on open doesn't _have_ to actually do anything, but in practice on Linux and the common ext4/xfs it does, and thus avoids weird crash->recover->power loss, and now storage is now ahead of the WAL sorts of weirdness.

Example:

title: [tracking] cypher conformance
body:
Noting down areas where our Cypher support does not conform with openCypher or Neo4j.

## Bugs:
- [ ] https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/5963
- [ ] https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/6010
- [ ] Incorrect precedence? ([TCK 1](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/precedence/Precedence3.feature#L72), [TCK 2](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/precedence/Precedence4.feature#L89))
```cypher
RETURN [1]+2 IN [3]+4 AS a,
             ([1]+2) IN ([3]+4) AS b,
             [1]+(2 IN [3])+4 AS c
Binder exception: Cannot match a built-in function for given function +(INT64[],BOOL).
```
- [ ] CREATE after MATCH ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/match/Match5.feature#L505))
```cypher
CREATE NODE TABLE N1(_k SERIAL PRIMARY KEY);
CREATE NODE TABLE N2(_k SERIAL PRIMARY KEY);
CREATE REL TABLE T(FROM N1 TO N2, FROM N2 TO N1);
CREATE (:N1)-[:T]->(:N2);
MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) CREATE (b)-[:T]->(a);
Binder exception: Create rel  bound by multiple node labels is not supported.

MATCH (a:A)-[r]->(b)
DELETE r
CREATE (b)-[:LIKES]->(a);
Binder exception: Create rel  bound by multiple node labels is not supported. 
```
Works for single node labels:
```cypher
CREATE NODE TABLE N(_k SERIAL PRIMARY KEY);
CREATE REL TABLE T(FROM N TO N);
CREATE (:N)-[:T]->(:N);
MATCH (a)-[r]->(b) CREATE (b)-[:T]->(a);
```
- [ ] Zero length paths are not returned ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/match/Match7.feature#L535)):
```cypher
CREATE NODE TABLE A(_k SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name STRING);
CREATE NODE TABLE B(_k SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name STRING);
CREATE NODE TABLE C(_k SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name STRING);
CREATE REL TABLE KNOWS(FROM A to B);
CREATE REL TABLE FRIEND(FROM B to C);

CREATE (a:A {name: 'A'})-[:KNOWS]->(b:B {name: 'B'})-[:FRIEND]->(c:C {name: 'C'});

MATCH p = (a {name: 'A'})-[:KNOWS*0..1]->(b)-[:FRIEND*0..1]->(c)
RETURN properties(list_distinct(nodes(p)), 'name') as p;
┌──────────┐
│ p        │
│ STRING[] │
├──────────┤
│ [A,B,C]  │
│ [A,B]    │
└──────────┘
```
Does not return `[A]` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/match/Match6.feature#L314)).
- [ ] https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/5989
- [ ] Optional Match after where is not supported ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/match/Match7.feature#L535)):
```cypher
MATCH (a)
WHERE NOT (a:B)
OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[r]->(a)
RETURN r
OPTIONAL>: expected rule oC_SingleQuery (line: 3, offset: 0)
"OPTIONAL MATCH (a)-[r]->(a)"
```
- [ ] Unexpected error `ORDER BY must be followed by SKIP or LIMIT` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/return/Return4.feature#L189)):
```cypher
MATCH (person:Person)<--(message)<-[like]-(:Person)
WITH like.creationDate AS likeTime, person AS person
  ORDER BY likeTime, message.id
WITH head(collect({likeTime: likeTime})) AS latestLike, person AS person
RETURN latestLike.likeTime AS likeTime
  ORDER BY likeTime
``` 
- [ ] Optional Match results in null ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/aggregation/Aggregation5.feature#L33)):
```cypher
CREATE NODE TABLE N(_k SERIAL PRIMARY KEY);

CREATE (:N);

MATCH (n)
OPTIONAL MATCH (n)-[:NOT_EXIST]->(x)
RETURN n, collect(x);

Actual: (:N) | null
Expected: (:N) | []
```
- [ ] Incorrect type inference ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/list/List5.feature#L37)):
```cypher
WITH [[1, 2, 3]] AS list
RETURN 3 IN list[1] AS r

Binder exception: Cannot compare INT64[] and INT64 in list_contains function.
```
- [ ] Incorrect cast to string when using size(): [TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/list/List6.feature#L94)
- [ ] Incorrect cast to bool: `MATCH (n) RETURN (n)-[]->()` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/pattern/Pattern1.feature#L412)).
- [ ] `RETURN [{}] AS literal`/`RETURN {a: {}} AS literal`/`RETURN {} AS literal` parser error ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/literals/Literals7.feature#L165))
- [ ] Incorrect handling of empty string search: `MATCH (a) WHERE a.name CONTAINS '' RETURN a` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/string/String10.feature#L71))

## Features
- [ ] `properties(n)/properties(r)` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/graph/Graph9.feature#L31))
- [ ] string functions:
  - [ ] `substring()` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/string/String1.feature#L31)).
  - [ ] `split()` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/string/String4.feature#L31)).
- [ ] `MATCH (n) WHERE n:LABEL`, `MATCH (n) WHERE n:$($param)` ([Neo4j](https://neo4j.com/docs/cypher-manual/current/clauses/where/#basic-filtering)).
- [ ] `MATCH (n) RETURN (n:Foo)`: where in RETURN ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/return/Return2.feature#L140))?
- [ ] `MATCH (n) SET n = $data` where `$data` is a dict containing property keys and values ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/set/Set4.feature#L42)).
- [ ] `MATCH (n:LABEL1|LABEL1)`/`MATCH ()-[:LABEL1|LABEL2]->()` https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/5807
- [ ] `list[1..3]` instead of `list[1:3]` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/list/List2.feature#L31)).
- [ ] Nested quantifiers: `WITH [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9] AS list RETURN single(x IN list WHERE none(y IN list WHERE x < y)) AS result` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/quantifier/Quantifier6.feature#L55))
- [ ] list comprehension:
    - [openCypher](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/main/tck/features/expressions/list/List12.feature)
    - [Neo4j](https://neo4j.com/docs/cypher-manual/current/expressions/list-expressions/#list-comprehension)
- [ ] Multiple labels on nodes https://github.com/kuzudb/kuzu/issues/3117
- [ ] DELETE from variable ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/delete/Delete5.feature#L31))
```cypher
MATCH (:User)-[:FRIEND]->(n)
WITH collect(n) AS friends
DETACH DELETE friends[1];

Binder exception: Cannot delete expression LIST_EXTRACT(friends,1) with type SCALAR_FUNCTION. Expect node or rel pattern.
```
- [ ] Deleting paths: `MATCH p = (:X)-->()-->()-->() DETACH DELETE p;` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/delete/Delete3.feature#L31))
- [ ] Delete undirected edges: `MATCH p = ()-[r:T]-() WHERE r.id = 42 DELETE r` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/delete/Delete2.feature#L31))
- [ ] Ordering lists: `Binder exception: Cannot order by lists. Order by STRING[] is not supported.` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/with-orderBy/WithOrderBy1.feature#L161))
- [ ] `min()` and `max()` [functions on lists](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/aggregation/Aggregation2.feature#L31).
- [ ] `percentileDisc()`, `percentileCont()` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/aggregation/Aggregation6.feature#L31)).
- [ ] `CREATE (a:N {name: 'A', num: 0, id: 0}),  (:N {name: 'B', num: a.id, id: 1})` fails due to `a.id` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/with-skip-limit/WithSkipLimit1.feature#L62)).
- [ ] Accessing variables in `WHERE` not declared in `WITH` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/with-where/WithWhere7.feature#L73)):
```cypher
MATCH (a)
WITH a.name2 AS name
WHERE name = 'B' OR a.name2 = 'C'
RETURN *
```
- [ ] Many datetime functions ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/temporal/Temporal1.feature#L31)):
  - [ ] `date({year: 1910, month: 5, day: 6})`
  - [ ] `localtime({hour: 12, minute: 31, second: 14, nanosecond: 645876123})`
  - [ ] `time({hour: 12, minute: 31, second: 14, nanosecond: 645876124, timezone: '+01:00'})`
  - [ ] `localdatetime({year: 9999, month: 9, day: 9, hour: 9, minute: 59, second: 59, nanosecond: 999999999})`
  - [ ] `datetime({year: 9999, month: 9, day: 9, hour: 9, minute: 59, second: 59, nanosecond: 999999999, timezone: '+11:59'})`
- [ ] explicit `CAST` functions ([Neo4j](https://neo4j.com/docs/cypher-manual/current/values-and-types/casting-data/)): `toInteger()`, `toFloat()`, etc
- [ ] Ternary comparisons ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/comparison/Comparison3.feature#L31)): `1 < n.num < 3`
- [ ] `WHERE exists { }` subquery ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/existentialSubqueries/ExistentialSubquery1.feature#L31)).
- [ ] `type()` function ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/graph/Graph4.feature#L31)).
- [ ] `RETURN [false, true] + false AS foo` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/list/List4.feature#L44)).
- [ ] `tail()` function on lists: [TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/list/List9.feature#L33)
- [ ] Support [hexadecimals](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/literals/Literals3.feature#L31) `RETURN -0x162CD4F6 AS literal` and [octals](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/literals/Literals4.feature#L31) `RETURN -0o2613152366 AS literal`.
- [ ] Scientific notation `1.2635418652381264e305`: [TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/literals/Literals5.feature#L85)
- [ ] Accessing maps keys using `[]` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/map/Map2.feature#L31))
- [ ] `keys()` function for structs: `RETURN keys({name: 'Alice', age: 38, address: {city: 'London', residential: true}})` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/map/Map3.feature#L37))

## Semantics
- [ ] Return empty instead of throwing error for reverse ranges: `MATCH (a)-[:LIKES*2..1]->(c)` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/match/Match5.feature#L238))
- [ ] Rounding up or down when casting: `WITH 82.9 AS weight RETURN cast(weight as int64)`. expected: `82`, actual: `83`. ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/typeConversion/TypeConversion2.feature#L33))
- [ ] `RETURN 1 AS a UNION RETURN 2 AS b` uses `a` as output column name (same as DuckDB). [TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/union/Union1.feature#L101) expects an column-name mismatch error.
- [ ] `null`s can be autocasted to ints (eg. `MERGE ({num: null})`). Should such casts be allowed? In [TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/clauses/merge/Merge1.feature#L300), the example throws an error.
- [ ] Handling properties of same name but different types ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/comparison/Comparison2.feature#L31)):
```cypher
CREATE NODE TABLE Root(_k SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, var INT64);
CREATE NODE TABLE Child(_k SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, var INT64);
CREATE REL TABLE T(FROM Root to Child);

CREATE (root:Root)-[:T]->(:Child {var: 0}),
         (root)-[:T]->(:Child {var: 'xx'}),
         (root)-[:T]->(:Child);

MATCH (:Root)-->(i:Child)
WHERE i.var IS NOT NULL AND i.var > 'x'
RETURN i.var

Query execution failed: Conversion exception: Cast failed. Could not convert "xx" to INT64.
``` 

- [ ] `null` semantics:
  - [ ] `collect()` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/aggregation/Aggregation8.feature#L61)): `UNWIND [null, null] AS x RETURN collect(DISTINCT x) AS c`. expected: [], actual: null`
  - [ ] ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/comparison/Comparison1.feature#L126)): `[null] = [1]`, `[[1], [2]] = [[1], [null]]`. expected: `null`, actual: `false`
  - [ ] `RETURN [1, 2] = [null, 2] AS res`. expected: `null`, actual: `false`
  - [ ] `RETURN [null] IN [[null]] AS res`. expected: null, actual: 
- [ ] `float` semantics:
  - [ ]  `nan` comparison ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/comparison/Comparison2.feature#L121)): `RETURN <lhs> > <rhs> AS gt, <lhs> >= <rhs> AS gtE, <lhs> < <rhs> AS lt, <lhs> <= <rhs> AS ltE`. expected: false | false | false | false, actual: false | false | true | true
  - [ ] `RETURN 1.34E999`. expected: FloatingPointOverflow, actual: `inf` ([TCK](https://github.com/opencypher/openCypher/blob/59edf2e1c17b845bf97c334ed06b2eb780950c13/tck/features/expressions/literals/Literals5.feature#L319))
